top_signals.title: Ukraine's Strike in Benghazi Threatens the Deal That Keeps Libya at Peace
top_signals.summary: Ukraine's sinking of a Russian warship in Benghazi on November 22 is the spark that could ignite another civil war in Libya, just as Tripoli is pitching foreign oil companies at an energy summit for the $20 billion it says it needs to lift output to 2 million barrels a day. Two officers of eastern strongman Khalifa Haftar's Libyan National Army (LNA) died of their wounds on November 24, and the LNA has vowed to retaliate "at the appropriate time and place." top_signals.title: NASA Wanted a 100-Kilowatt Reactor on the Moon but Is Settling for 20
top_signals.summary: In August 2025, Washington promised a 100-kilowatt nuclear reactor on the Moon by 2030, ahead of China and Russia. "We're in a race to the moon, in a race with China to the moon," NASA's then-interim chief Sean Duffy said, warning that whoever landed a reactor first could declare a "keep-out zone" around it. But the reactor NASA put out to bid on November 23 is one-fifth that size. top_signals.title: EU Budget Talks Break Down; Spain Set to Vote
top_signals.summary:
European Union leaders cut budget talks short during a summit in Brussels after frustrated countries refused to budge in negotiations over the bloc’s long-term funding plan. Meanwhile, Spaniards prepare to vote in a general election on Sunday, with Prime Minister Pedro Sánchez fighting to stay in office.

top_signals.title: Widespread PHP Flaw May Cause Many Site Outages Today
top_signals.summary: Expect to see quite a few websites serving "404" or "Page Not Found" errors today: Nearly 70 percent of websites need to update their core software to fix a pair of vulnerabilities that allow an attacker to seize full control over affected servers. Experts say there are working exploits for the flaws, and that these critical bugs are already being exploited in the wild.
